summary: Source-based expansion of ECD §26 (adic coefficients: Definition 26.1, Proposition 26.2 via Bhatt-Scholze derived completeness, the six operations for I-adic Λ by passage to the limit over Λ/I^n, Remark 26.3) and §27 (comparison to schemes: the v-sheaf X^◇ of a characteristic-p scheme and its mixed-characteristic variant over a complete DVR, the comparison functor c_X^*, Propositions 27.1-27.7 with their proofs as written), together with the statements and proof strategies of de Jong's alteration theorems 4.1, 5.8 and 6.5 that 27.6 invokes. nodes.title: D_ét(Y,Λ) for I-adically complete Λ: definition, ∞-categorical enhancement and the inverse-limit description (ECD 26.1-26.2, via Bhatt-Scholze)
nodes.statement: Coefficients: a ring Λ complete for the I-adic topology, I ⊆ Λ finitely generated, assumed generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p. Definition 26.1: for a small v-stack Y, D_ét(Y,Λ) ⊆ D(Y_v, Λ) is the full subcategory of derived I-complete A (in the sense of [BS15, Definition 3.4.1, Lemma 3.4.12]: for each U and x ∈ I(U), T(A|U, x) = R lim(... -> A -x-> A -x-> A) vanishes; equivalently A ≅ R lim of the Koszul reductions along generators of I) with A ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ/I). Proposition 26.2: there is a presentable stable ∞-category D_ét(Y,Λ) with this homotopy category, given as the full ∞-subcategory of D(Y_v,Λ) on those objects, and D_ét(Y,Λ) -> lim_n D_ét(Y, Λ/I^n) is an equivalence; the inclusion into D(Y_v,Λ) does not preserve all colimits (colimits must be completed). Proof: by [Lur09, 5.5.3.13] it suffices that D_ét(Y,Λ) -> lim_n D_ét(Y,Λ/I^n) is an equivalence, which follows from the equivalence D_comp(Y_v,Λ) -> lim_n D(Y_v, Λ/I^n) of [BS15, Lemma 3.5.7] — where BS15 assumes Λ noetherian but, as ECD notes, noetherianity is unnecessary when I is generated by a regular sequence (BS15's 3.5.7(5) is the unbounded extension 'if m is regular').
hypotheses: Λ I-adically complete, I generated by a regular sequence and containing an integer prime to p (the last condition makes the Λ/I-theory available)
Bhatt-Scholze 3.5.7 is stated for a noetherian R and a replete topos; ECD drops noetherianity citing the regular-sequence hypothesis; BS15 Lemma 3.5.5 (used in the proof of 3.5.7(3)) was not read
proofSteps: Define derived I-completeness on the v-site (BS15 3.4.1/3.4.12).

Use π: (C, Λ_•) -> (Y_v, Λ) (BS15 3.5.7(1)) with π^* A = {A ⊗^L Λ/I^n}, π_* {A_n} = R lim A_n; full faithfulness of π^* from A ≅ R lim(A ⊗^L Λ/I^n) for complete A (BS15 3.5.1); the equivalence via 3.5.5 and the regular case (5).
Apply Lurie 5.5.3.13 for presentability of the limit of presentable categories.

nodes.title: The six operations on D_ét(Y,Λ) for adic Λ and their reduction modulo I (ECD §26 text and Remark 26.3)
nodes.statement: f^*: D_ét(Y,Λ) -> D_ét(Y',Λ) is the restriction of f_v^* (which preserves completeness, commuting with all limits, and reduction modulo I); f^* preserves direct sums (checked modulo I), so it has a right adjoint Rf_*; the completed tensor product − ⊗̂^L_Λ − is the completion of the v-site tensor product and RHom_Λ is its adjoint. Rf_! for f compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞ is built by running the construction for the pro-system (Λ/I^n)_n and passing to the limit; it preserves direct sums and has an ∞-enhancement, hence a right adjoint Rf^!. Remark 26.3: f^*, Rf_!, ⊗̂ are compatible with D_ét(Y,Λ) ≅ lim_n D_ét(Y,Λ/I^n); Rf_*, Rf^!, RHom commute with − ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I because I is generated by a regular sequence and the functors are exact, hence by induction with − ⊗^L Λ/I^n, so they are limits of the finite-level operations; consequently any natural transformation (e.g. a base change map) is an equivalence iff it is so modulo I, and all introductory theorems hold for adic Λ.
hypotheses: Same Λ, I as in the previous node; the geometric hypotheses on f for Rf_! are unchanged from the torsion case (compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, locally finite dim.trg)

nodes.title: The small v-sheaf X^◇ of a characteristic-p scheme, the morphism of sites c_X and the comparison functor c_X^* (ECD §27 opening)
nodes.statement: For a scheme X of characteristic p, X^◇ is the small v-sheaf S ↦ Hom(S, X) in adic spaces, where schemes are embedded via Spec R ↦ Spa(R, R^+) with R^+ the integral closure of F_p in R; the functor factors through perfect schemes. It induces a functor of sites c_X: X^◇_v -> X_ét and, for a discrete ring Λ, c_X^*: D(X_ét,Λ) -> D_ét(X^◇,Λ). For an adic Λ as in §26 (I regular, containing an integer prime to p) one works on the pro-étale site: c_X: X^◇_v -> X_proét, and completed pullback gives c_X^*: D_ét(X,Λ) -> D_ét(X^◇,Λ), where D_ét(X,Λ) ⊆ D(X_proét,Λ) consists of the derived I-complete A with A ⊗^L Λ/I in the left completion D̂(X_ét,Λ) ⊆ D(X_proét,Λ) (equivalently all cohomology sheaves in the essential image of X~_ét); when D(X_ét,Λ) is left-complete (e.g. finite cohomological dimension) this is A ⊗^L Λ/I ∈ D(X_ét,Λ). Proposition 27.1: c_X^* commutes with ⊗̂^L and with pullback: (f^◇)^* c_X^* = c_Y^* f^* ('clear from the definition').
hypotheses: X any scheme of characteristic p; the plus-ring convention (integral closure of F_p) is part of the definition
The source asserts, without proof, that X^◇ is a small v-sheaf, that it factors through perfection, and that c_X is a morphism of sites
proofSteps: Define X^◇; note the factorization through perfection; define c_X and its pro-étale variant; check 27.1 from definitions.
acceptance: For X = Spec k with k a perfect field of characteristic p, X^◇ = Spd(k, k^+) with k^+ the integral closure of F_p in k — not Spd(k,k) (contrast with the mixed-characteristic convention).
Both c_X^* and (f^◇)^* are defined on the v-site and compatible (27.1(ii)).

nodes.title: The diamond X^◇ over Spd O of a scheme locally of finite type over a complete DVR O with perfect residue field, and its incompatibility with the characteristic-p convention (ECD §27, before 27.5)
nodes.statement: Fix a complete discrete valuation ring O with perfect residue field k and X locally of finite type over Spec O. X^◇ is the functor on perfectoid spaces S of characteristic p sending S to the set of untilts S^♯ over Spa O = Spa(O,O) together with a map S^♯ -> X of locally ringed spaces over Spec O; it is a diamond over Spd O. This is not compatible with the characteristic-p functor: Spec k is sent to Spd k = Spd(k,k), not Spd(k,k^+). As before one obtains c_X^*: D_ét(X,Λ) -> D_ét(X^◇,Λ) satisfying 27.1, commuting with colimits, with right adjoint Rc_{X*} satisfying 27.3.
hypotheses: O a complete DVR with perfect residue field; X locally of finite type over O (the source: 'we have to impose stronger finiteness hypothesis')
That X^◇ is a diamond over Spd O is asserted, not proved, in the read text (the affine relative representability is the R1 'relative representability statements used in 27.5' of the stage)
proofSteps: Define via untilts over Spa(O,O) and maps of locally ringed spaces; note the convention clash; define c_X^* and Rc_{X*}.
acceptance: The generic fibre: for X = Spec K, X^◇ = Spd K (used in 27.7's Galois-cohomology comparison).
Comparison maps between the two conventions exist only where the plus rings agree; never identify Spd(k,k) with Spd(k,k^+).

nodes.title: What 27.4-27.6 require from scheme compactification: Nagata factorisation, filteredness of factorisations, and reduction to finitely presented proper maps
nodes.statement: The proof of 27.4 uses: (a) Nagata's compactification theorem to write a separated finite-type map f of qcqs characteristic-p schemes as an open immersion followed by a proper map; (b) that any two such factorisations are dominated by a third (the category of factorisations is filtered), so that the construction of the comparison for Rf_! is essentially independent of the choice; (c) for proper f, base change to F̄_p and reduction to affine X, then factorisation of f into a closed immersion and a proper map of finite presentation, reducing to finitely presented f; (d) a Postnikov-limit reduction to A ∈ D^{≥0}, then to constructible A, and then, since the situation is a base change from finite-type X, Y, reduction to that case. 27.6 also compactifies X over O ('we assume that X is proper over O (by compactifying)'). None of these scheme statements is proved in ECD; the Stacks Project references named by the stage were not read.
hypotheses: qcqs schemes of characteristic p (27.4) or schemes of finite type over O (27.5-27.6); separated finite-type morphisms
Nagata compactification for qcqs schemes, closed-immersion/finite-presentation factorisation and the filteredness of factorisations are imported without proof
proofSteps: Record the exact usage; source the statements from the Stacks Project (Tags 0F41, 0A9Z for Nagata over qcqs bases) in a later pass.
acceptance: The Rf_! comparison in 27.4 must be shown independent of the factorisation; the source only remarks that the category of factorisations is filtered.

sources.excerpt: By Nagata's compactification theorem, one can write f as a composite of an open immersion and a proper map. Moreover, any two such factorizations are dominated by a third map (in fact, the category of factorizations is filtered), which makes the following construction essentially independent of the choice.
sources.match: The compactification input and the independence remark.

sources.excerpt: Also we may factor f into a closed immersion and a proper map of finite presentation, which reduces us to the case that f is finitely presented.

nodes.title: Full faithfulness of c_X^*: D_ét(X,Λ) -> D_ét(X^◇,Λ) for schemes of characteristic p (ECD Proposition 27.2) with the perfected-affine-space, exhaustion-by-balls and radius arguments
nodes.statement: For any scheme X of characteristic p, c_X^* is fully faithful and admits a right adjoint Rc_{X*}. Proof as printed: Rc_{X*} exists by the adjoint functor theorem and commutes with derived reduction modulo I (exactness, I regular) and agrees with the Λ/I-adjoint on D_ét(X^◇,Λ/I); the unit A -> Rc_{X*}c_X^*A being an isomorphism can be checked modulo I, so assume Λ discrete killed by n prime to p; by Postnikov limits assume A ∈ D^+_ét(X,Λ) = D^+(X_ét,Λ); checking on a basis of étale U reduces to RΓ(X,A) = RΓ(X^◇, c_X^*A); by descent assume X affine over F̄_p and, via a closed embedding, X = Spec F̄_p[X_i^{1/p^∞}, i ∈ I] (I possibly infinite) and Λ = F_ℓ. Let C be the completed algebraic closure of F̄_p((t)). By invariance of étale cohomology under change of algebraically closed base field, RΓ(X,A) = RΓ(X_C,A); by Theorem 19.5, RΓ(X^◇, c_X^*A) = RΓ(X_C^◇, c_X^*A) with X_C^◇ = X^◇ ×_{Spd F̄_p} Spd C. Write X_C^◇ as a filtered colimit of infinite-dimensional balls X_{C,(n_i)} = Spd C⟨(t^{n_i}X_i)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (n_i powers of p), so RΓ(X_C^◇, c_X^*A) = R lim RΓ(X_{C,(n_i)}, c_X^*A), and it suffices that RΓ(X,A) -> RΓ(X_{C,(n_i)}, c_X^*A) is an isomorphism for each choice; both sides commute with filtered colimits in A, so assume A constructible, hence pulled back from a finite-dimensional affine space; reduce to I finite and all n_i = 1 by adjoining p-power roots. For n ∈ Z[1/p]_{>0} let X_{C,n} be the ball with all n_i = n: automorphisms of C over F̄_p sending t to t^n give X_{C,n} ≅ X_{C,1} compatibly with the map to X^◇, so RΓ(X_{C,n}, c_X^*A) is abstractly independent of n; by [Hub96, Proposition 6.1.1] each RΓ(X_{C,n}, c_X^*A) has finite total dimension; since c_X^*A is overconvergent, RΓ(X_{C,1}, c_X^*A) = colim_{n>1} RΓ(X_{C,n}, c_X^*A), so for n > 1 close to 1 the restriction RΓ(X_{C,n}, ·) -> RΓ(X_{C,1}, ·) is surjective in each degree, hence an isomorphism (equal finite cardinalities); applying the automorphisms, all RΓ(X_{C,n^j}, ·) -> RΓ(X_{C,1}, ·) are isomorphisms, so RΓ(X_C^◇, c_X^*A) = RΓ(X_{C,1}, c_X^*A); finally, identifying X_C^◇ with the diamond of the rigid space over C attached to X_C (Lemma 15.6) and using [Hub96, Theorem 3.8.1], RΓ(X_C, A) -> RΓ(X_C^◇, c_X^*A) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: X any scheme of characteristic p; Λ as in §26 (I regular, containing n prime to p); after reduction Λ = F_ℓ, ℓ ≠ p

Imports: Theorem 19.5 (fully faithful pullback under extension of algebraically closed base fields; statement read), invariance of scheme étale cohomology under algebraically closed extension (not sourced in the read text), Huber 6.1.1 (finiteness for constructible sheaves on quasi-compact spaces locally of algebraically finite type over an affinoid field, statement read), Huber 3.8.1 (comparison for finite-type k-schemes, statement read), Lemma 15.6 (read), overconvergence of c_X^*A (not sourced in the read text)
proofSteps: Adjoint functor theorem and reduction modulo I.
Reduction to perfected affine space over F̄_p with F_ℓ-coefficients.
Base change to C and Theorem 19.5.
Exhaustion by balls and finite-stage constructibility.
Radius argument via automorphisms of C, finiteness 6.1.1 and overconvergence.
Classical comparison 3.8.1 via Lemma 15.6.
acceptance: The restriction maps in the radius argument are the actual cohomology restriction maps; the abstract isomorphisms X_{C,n} ≅ X_{C,1} are used only to transport the surjectivity statement, as the stage demands.
Full faithfulness is a statement about D_ét, not an equivalence: essential surjectivity is not claimed.

sources.excerpt: If X is any scheme of characteristic p, the functor c_X^*: D_ét(X, Λ) -> D_ét(X^◇, Λ) is fully faithful and admits a right adjoint Rc_{X*}.

Moreover, by [Hub96, Proposition 6.1.1], we know that for each n, the cohomology RΓ(X_{C,n}, c_X^*A) is of finite total dimension. On the other hand, as c_X^*A is overconvergent, we have RΓ(X_{C,1}, c_X^*A) = lim RΓ(X_{C,n}, c_X^*A).

But by the identification of X_C^◇ with the diamond associated to the rigid space to C associated to X_C and [Hub96, Theorem 3.8.1], we know that the natural map RΓ(X_C, A) -> RΓ(X_C^◇, c_X^*A) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: de Jong's Theorem 4.1: alteration of a variety over a field to a regular projective variety with strict normal crossings boundary, with its reduction strategy
nodes.statement: Theorem 4.1: for a variety X over a field k and a proper closed subset Z ⊆ X there exist an alteration φ_1: X_1 -> X and an open immersion j_1: X_1 -> X̄_1 such that (i) X̄_1 is a projective variety and a regular scheme, and (ii) j_1(φ_1^{-1}(Z)) ∪ (X̄_1 − j_1(X_1)) is a strict normal crossings divisor in X̄_1; if k is perfect, φ_1 may be chosen generically étale. Remark 4.2: X_1 -> Spec k factors through a finite extension k_1 with X̄_1 geometrically irreducible and smooth over k_1; for perfect k, X_1 is smooth over k. Proof strategy read (4.3-4.11): induction on dim X (dim 0 trivial; dim 1 by normalization); successive reductions preserving the problem under alterations (4.4): (i) k algebraically closed (4.5, descending a solution over k̄ to a finite k_1 ⊆ k̄); (ii) X quasi-projective (Chow's lemma, 4.6); (iii) X projective (compactify and restrict, 4.7); (iv) Z the support of a divisor (blow up Z, 4.8); Z may be enlarged (4.9); (v) X normal (normalization, 4.10). Lemma 4.11: for (X,Z) satisfying (i)-(iv) there is a modification φ: X' -> X (blow-up of a finite set S of regular closed points disjoint from Z) and a morphism f: X' -> P^{d-1} with all fibres nonempty equidimensional of dimension 1, smooth locus dense in all fibres, f|Z' finite and étale over an open of P^{d-1}, and (if X is normal) at least one smooth fibre — proved by a generic linear projection π: X -> P^d adapted to Z (2.11) and a general point p ∉ B ∪ π(Z), with X' = {(x,t): π(x) ∈ t} and Bertini for the last clause. Steps 4.12-4.22 (application of the curve theorem to f and the final construction) were not read.
hypotheses: X a variety over a field k (integral, separated, finite type); Z proper closed; alterations are proper dominant generically finite maps (de Jong's §2)
Generic étaleness of φ_1 only for perfect k
Steps 4.12-4.22 and the curve-fibration input (Theorem 5.8 / stable reduction) not read
proofSteps: Reductions (i)-(v) as listed.
Construct the curve fibration f: X' -> P^{d-1} (Lemma 4.11).
(Not read) apply Theorem 5.8 / semistable reduction to f, use induction on d for the base, and assemble X̄_1.
acceptance: The boundary divisor includes both the preimage of Z and the complement of X_1 in X̄_1.
No resolution of singularities is used; the output is an alteration, generically étale only when k is perfect.

sources.excerpt: There exist an alteration φ_1: X_1 -> X and an open immersion j_1: X_1 -> X̄_1 such that (i) X̄_1 is a projective variety and is a regular scheme, and (ii) the closed subset j_1(φ_1^{-1}(Z)) ∪ X̄_1 \ j_1(X_1) is a strict normal crossings divisor in X̄_1. If k is perfect then the alteration φ_1 may be chosen to be generically étale.
We proceed step by step, each time reducing the theorem to a case where we have additional restaints, numbered (i), (ii), etc., on the pair (X, Z).
(ii) a) All fibres of f are equidimensional of dimension 1 and nonempty. b) The smooth locus of f is dense in all fibres of f.

nodes.title: de Jong's Theorem 5.8: alteration of a projective curve fibration to a split semi-stable curve with sections controlling a closed subset (statement and strategy)
nodes.statement: Theorem 5.8: let f: X -> S be a projective morphism of integral excellent schemes with all fibres nonempty and equidimensional of dimension 1 and smooth locus dense in all fibres. There is a diagram X_1 -> X over S_1 -> S with ψ: S_1 -> S and φ_1: X_1 -> X alterations and f_1: X_1 -> S_1 a projective split semi-stable curve with smooth generic fibre; given a proper closed subset Z ⊆ X, one may choose the diagram with mutually disjoint sections σ_1..σ_n of f_1 into sm(X_1/S_1) and a divisor D_1 ⊆ S_1 such that φ_1^{-1}(Z) is contained in f_1^{-1}(D_1) ∪ σ_1(S_1) ∪ ... ∪ σ_n(S_1) (display OCR-garbled; reconstructed from 5.9-5.10 and the statement's prose). Strategy (5.9-5.10): as for 4.1, replace S by alterations S' -> S and X by an irreducible component X' of X ×_S S' dominating X (a) and b) persist); make the generic fibre geometrically a union of smooth irreducible curves after a finite extension of the function field (5.10), normalize, and continue (not read further).
hypotheses: f projective; X, S integral excellent; fibres nonempty, equidimensional of dimension 1 with dense smooth locus
Proof beyond 5.10 not read
proofSteps: Alteration of the base and passage to a dominating component; normalization; (unread) three-point-stabilisation and the stable reduction of the generic curve.
acceptance: The output curve is split semi-stable with smooth generic fibre and comes with disjoint sections in the smooth locus.
The degree of the alteration is not controlled (it may be divisible by ℓ), as the stage warns.

Here X' is an irreducible component of X ×_S S' dominating X. (Such a component exists, as ψ is finite flat over a nonempty open part of S.)

nodes.title: de Jong's Theorem 6.5: strictly semi-stable alteration over a trait after finite base extension; strict semi-stable pairs (6.3), their local form (6.4) and strictly semi-stable S-varieties (2.16)
nodes.statement: Setting: S a trait (spectrum of a (complete) DVR, 2.12), X an S-variety, Z ⊆ X a proper closed subset containing the special fibre f^{-1}(s). Definitions: X is strictly semi-stable over S (2.16) if the generic fibre is smooth, the special fibre X_s is reduced with irreducible components X_i that are divisors on X, and every intersection X_J (J ≠ ∅) is smooth over κ(s) of codimension #J; locally X is then smooth over Spec R[t_1..t_r]/(t_1···t_r − π). (X,Z) is a strict semi-stable pair (6.3) if X is strictly semi-stable, Z is a strict normal crossings divisor, and for the flat part Z_f = ∪ Z_j every Z_J is a disjoint union of strictly semi-stable S-varieties; locally (6.4) the complete local ring is C[[t_1..t_n, s_1..s_m]]/(π − t_1···t_n) with C formally smooth over R, Z_j = {s_j = 0}, X_i = {t_i = 0}. Theorem 6.5: there exist a trait S_1 finite over S, an S_1-variety X_1, an alteration φ_1: X_1 -> X over S and an open immersion j_1: X_1 -> X̄_1 of S_1-varieties such that (i) X̄_1 is a projective S_1-variety with geometrically irreducible generic fibre and (ii) (X̄_1, j_1(φ_1^{-1}(Z)) ∪ (X̄_1 − j_1(X_1))) is a strict semi-stable pair. Strategy read (6.7-6.9): induction on the relative dimension; reductions to X projective over S and Z the support of a divisor as in 4.6-4.8; finite base change of traits S' -> S with X' an irreducible component of X_{S'} (6.8); a finite extension of R(S) making the generic fibre geometrically reduced and irreducible (6.9). Steps 6.10-6.14 (application of Theorem 5.8 to the curve fibration and the final construction) not read.
hypotheses: S a trait; X an S-variety; Z ⊇ f^{-1}(s) a proper closed subset
The finite extension S_1/S is part of the conclusion and cannot be avoided
6.10-6.14 not read
proofSteps: Reductions 6.7-6.9.
(Not read) curve fibration and Theorem 5.8; induction on relative dimension; strict semi-stability of the result.
acceptance: Strict semi-stability implies regularity of X (remark after 2.16).
The local model C[[t,s]]/(π − t_1···t_n) is the input for the explicit nearby-cycle computations of 27.6.

nodes.title: Commutation of c_X^* with Rf_* for separated finite-type maps over O on constructible complexes with finite prime-to-p coefficients (ECD Proposition 27.6): the dévissage and alteration route
nodes.statement: For f: Y -> X separated between schemes of finite type over O and Λ a finite ring killed by an integer prime to p, for every constructible complex A of Λ-modules on Y_ét the map c_X^* Rf_* A -> Rf^◇_* c_Y^* A is an isomorphism. Proof as printed: factor f as an open immersion followed by a proper map; the proper case is 27.5; so assume f = j: U -> X an open immersion; dévissage to A = F_ℓ constant and either U inside the generic fibre (p ≠ 0) or U of characteristic p. Characteristic p: by de Jong's alterations [dJ96, 4.1, 6.5], after replacing k by a finite extension, reduce to the boundary Z being a normal crossings divisor over k; as in 27.5 it suffices to prove the result after pullback along T -> Spa O; the right side is Rj_{T*}F_ℓ for the analytic open immersion j_T: U_T -> X_T; both Rj_*F_ℓ and Rj_{T*}F_ℓ are computed explicitly (via Ri^!F_ℓ and Ri_T^!F_ℓ for the strata i: Z -> X, smooth over k) and the comparison is an isomorphism. Generic fibre: assume X proper over O (compactify) and factor j as U -> X_η followed by X_η -> X; the first is handled as before by alterations (or resolution in characteristic 0); for X_η -> X, by alterations after replacing O by a finite extension assume X strictly semistable; by induction on dimension and smooth pullback the map is an isomorphism away from a finite set of k-points (the most singular points); it then suffices to check after proper pushforward along X -> Spec O, where commutation is known (27.5), reducing to the open immersion Spec K -> Spec O, 'handled by a direct computation'.
hypotheses: f separated between finite-type O-schemes; Λ finite killed by an integer prime to p; A constructible
The 'explicit' purity/Kummer computations for normal crossings strata, the smooth-pullback/dimension-induction step, and the direct computation for Spec K -> Spec O are not written in the source
Replacing k or O by a finite extension is allowed by the alteration theorems and must be compatible with the comparison (not discussed in the source)
proofSteps: Nagata + 27.5 for the proper part.
Dévissage to constant F_ℓ on opens in the special or generic fibre.
Alterations (4.1 in char p; 6.5 over O) to normal-crossing / strictly semistable situations; pullback to T; explicit local computations.
Induction on dimension and reduction to Spec K -> Spec O via proper pushforward.
acceptance: An alteration may have degree divisible by ℓ; the argument as printed does not use a trace splitting but the explicit local computations after alteration — the descent step from the altered situation back to X is not spelled out in the source and must be supplied (cohomological descent along proper hypercovers, per the stage).
The coefficient ring is finite and prime-to-p; no p-torsion claim.

sources.excerpt: Let f: Y -> X be a separated map between schemes of finite type over O, and assume that Λ is a finite ring killed by an integer prime to p. Then for any constructible complex A of Λ-modules on Y_ét, the map c_X^* Rf_* A -> Rf^◇_* c_Y^* A is an isomorphism.

In characteristic p, by an application of de Jong's alterations, [dJ96, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 6.5], we can, up to replacing k by a finite extension, reduce to the case that the boundary Z is a normal crossing divisor over k.
this reduces us to the open immersion Spec K -> Spec O. This can be handled by a direct computation.

nodes.title: Full faithfulness of c_X^* on constructible complexes for schemes locally of finite type over O (ECD Proposition 27.7)
nodes.statement: Assume Λ is a finite ring (the proof uses 27.6, hence the standing prime-to-p hypothesis). For X locally of finite type over O and A a constructible complex of Λ-modules on X_ét, A -> Rc_{X*}c_X^*A is an isomorphism. Proof: for X = Spec O, allowing a finite cover of O, it suffices to treat A = Z/nZ and A = i_*Z/nZ (i the closed point); the second is simple; the first reduces to Rj_*F_ℓ, and by 27.6 the claim becomes that RΓ(Spec K, F_ℓ) -> RΓ(Spd K, F_ℓ) is an isomorphism, both sides being Galois cohomology. In general check on global sections: RΓ(X,−) = RΓ(Spec O, Rf_*−) for f: X -> Spec O and 27.6 reduce to the base.
hypotheses: Λ finite; the proof passes through 27.6 and therefore needs Λ killed by an integer prime to p — the stage's reading that 'finite ring' in 27.7 does not extend the coefficient scope is confirmed by the proof
The identification of RΓ(Spd K, F_ℓ) with Galois cohomology of K is asserted
proofSteps: Base case Spec O by dévissage to Z/nZ and i_*Z/nZ; use 27.6 and Galois cohomology.
General X via global sections and 27.6.
acceptance: For A = F_ℓ on Spec O the statement is H^i(Spec K, F_ℓ) = H^i(Spd K, F_ℓ).

sources.excerpt: Assume that Λ is a finite ring. Then for any scheme X locally of finite type over O and any constructible complex A of Λ-modules on X_ét, the adjunction map A -> Rc_{X*}c_X^*A is an isomorphism.
Using Proposition 27.6, the claim then becomes that RΓ(Spec K, F_ℓ) -> RΓ(Spd K, F_ℓ) is an isomorphism, where K is the quotient field of O, but here both sides are Galois cohomology.
